findings.text: the sourcing guard is not equivalent to the reader it guards, so it refuses three shapes engine_metrics accepts. _has_sample_line peels the line by hand (line 121 `if not line.startswith(prefix): continue`, line 129 `elif rest[:1] == " "`, line 131 the else branch that treats any other separator as a longer series name), while the reader it stands for calls `line = raw_line.strip()` (imas_ambix/agent/engine_metrics.py:218) and matches `\s+` (:46). Concrete input: the fixture's own requests_running line indented by one space, ` sglang:num_running_reqs{engine_type="unified",model_name="deepseek-v4.1-flash",moe_ep_rank="0",pp_rank="0",tp_rank="0"} 0.0`. Measured on the real fixture text with that one line rewritten: engine_metrics resolves requests_running (True) while _has_sample_line returns False. Same divergence for a leading tab and for a leading narrow no-break space. On the UNLABELLED branch the divergence is a bare tab: input `sglang:num_running_reqs\t0.0`, module parse_metrics -> [('sglang:num_running_reqs', {}, 0.0)], guard -> False. So a scrape that carries every canonical field and is indented or tab-separated anywhere reddens this test with the message 'unsourced' for fields that both instruments can read, which is a false red traced to the guard rather than to the fixture. Empty label set, timestamp column and trailing comment were measured too and are handled correctly (module True, guard True).

the receipt's restoration line is evaluated before the restoration it names, so it is a constant rather than a measurement: it reads `--- test file restored byte-identically: NO`. The block that writes the log ends at `} > "$R/neg-control-unlabelled-branch.log"` and the restore is the NEXT command (`cp /tmp/r4b-test.bak "$F"; diff -q ...`), so the `cmp -s` ran against the still-mutated file and can print nothing else. The manifest contradicts it: evidence_inputs item 11(a) states 'The test file was restored byte-identically (sha256 verified)' and cites this receipt. The underlying claim is in fact TRUE and I verified it independently at the reviewed head - the worktree file's sha256 851e64bcd3c39844f8feca13ac3faed5042c70da6945dd0794a4330c0e4639ee equals /tmp/r4b-test.bak's (22388 bytes, `cmp` exit 0) and equals `git show HEAD:tests/test_engine_metrics.py` - but no receipt in the run directory holds that fact, so a reader of the log alone concludes the opposite.

this receipt mutates the same test file in place and records no restoration line at all, while the manifest's evidence_inputs item 10(a) makes the same claim for it ('The file was restored byte-identically (sha256 verified)'). The log ends at the short test summary. The restore is real - the two in-place mutations left the file byte-identical to its pre-mutation bytes - but the verification the manifest cites is not in the receipt, so the run's two in-place mutations are evidenced by the final state rather than by either log.

one assertion still derives its expected value from the module under test, which is this sprint's recurring defect left standing in the one test the round did not convert. `_published(family)` (line 219-224, docstring 'read from its own series tables') builds the expectation from engine_metrics.GAUGE_SERIES and COUNTER_SERIES, and line 389 compares the delivered vLLM key set to an `expected_vllm` built from those same two tables (lines 378-381). Demonstrated by doing it: with `engine_metrics.GAUGE_SERIES.pop("requests_running")` applied at conftest import, test_both_families_report_every_quantity_they_publish stays GREEN (1 passed, 15 deselected) while test_the_recorded_scrape_sources_every_canonical_field reddens on the same removal - so the reader can stop publishing a canonical quantity for both families and the derived pair shrinks silently and the whole file has gone green. The written-out literal at lines 55-97 is what catches it, which confirms the record's own diagnosis in evidence_inputs item 4 that the gap was closed on the SGLang canonical set only.

justifications.durability: the unlabelled branch is now genuinely pinned and I measured it rather than trusting the receipt: applying ca25efb8's recorded mutation verbatim to a scratch copy of the head test file (tests/test_engine_metrics.py:130 `labels, value = "", rest` -> `labels, value = "", ""`) turns exactly one test red, `FAILED ...::test_a_series_name_without_a_value_is_not_a_source`, 1 failed, 15 deselected - the same count the receipt records - while the unmutated head copy is 16 passed; the label-bearing branch and both positives are asserted in the same test, so both spellings of a sample line are now held independently and the unlabelled branch cannot be neutralised unnoticed. Docked three because the guard itself is not a faithful model of the reader it guards: three shapes the reader accepts (leading space, leading tab, leading no-break space) and one unlabelled spelling the reader accepts (a bare tab separator) are refused, so the test's 'unsourced' verdict is not the reader's verdict and its false reds point at the fixture rather than at the check.
justifications.evidence: the declared control reproduces under my own hand and its assertion is specific: dropping the requests_running sample line from a COPY of the stored scrape (worktree fixture sha256 8756c081509719472f1fff0260011955705ddb9a788a7189131119f017f47a49, identical before and after; the copy moved to b2c4bfc4a9cb8560a68211c33743fd6e0fbef23354ed1d35c3b6bf70e57d4c6f) gives 1 failed, 15 deselected, exit 1, with {'unresolved': ['requests running (requests_running)'], 'unsourced': ['requests running (requests_running)'], ...} - the receipt's own text. Both load-bearing receipts replay to their recorded counts at 7adfc3a3: the gauge reader mutation gives 6 failed, 10 passed exactly as neg-control-canonical-field-dropped's subject says

Review of run r-20260921T053443850077-scrape-fixture at its round-five head 7adfc3a3, plan imas-ambix:serve-telemetry-spine section 2, fifth review round. Reviewed base 38151b74 (the fourth round's head; the run's own base is 39e7bba5), reviewed commit 7adfc3a30700563e659b54999153df6d00c90dc3 (worktree head, clean, fixture blob untouched). The worktree was cut from the reviewed head, which I read in place and report here.

CHECKLIST 1 - every control log in the run directory replayed by this reviewer, not taken on the worker's account.

(a) negative_control.log, the declared control (fixture side). Replayed as specified: I removed the requests_running sample line from a copy of tests/data/sglang_metrics_sample.txt and ran the current selector against it. Result 1 failed, 15 deselected, exit 1, assertion {'unresolved': ['requests running (requests_running)'], 'unsourced': ['requests running (requests_running) <- num_running_reqs']} - the receipt's own text. The worktree fixture is byte-identical before and after (sha256 8756c081...), so the stored scrape is unmutated and is still the authority.

(b) neg-control-canonical-field-dropped.log (reader side). Replayed verbatim: GAUGE_SERIES['requests_running'][FAMILY_SGLANG] -> ('num_running_reqs_renamed',). Result 6 failed, 10 passed - the receipt's recorded count, reproduced at the reviewed head.

(c) neg-control-unlabelled-branch.log. Replayed verbatim: tests/test_engine_metrics.py:130 `labels, value = "", rest` -> `labels, value = "", ""`. Result 0 failed, 15 deselected at exit 1 - the recorded count. But this log's own last line, `--- test file restored byte-identically: NO`, is a constant: the restore is the command AFTER the block that closes the log, so the cmp ran against the still-mutated file. The manifest claims sha256 verification for this restore; no receipt holds it. I verified the state independently and it is correct.

(d) neg-control-pre-fix-sample-line.log, neg-control-counter-series-dropped.log, neg-control-histogram-series-dropped.log, neg-control-storage-tier-dropped.log. Read at the head; the test-file-touching one carries no restoration line at all (same manifest claim, same absence). The three reader receipts mutate module tables in memory and need no restore. Their counts are consistent with the mutation driver's own scope and I did not re-derive each one.

CHECKLIST 2 - a third exposition shape. Found: the guard refuses four shapes the reader accepts. INPUT, leader space: ` sglang:num_running_reqs{engine_type="unified",model_name="deepseek-v4.1-flash",moe_ep_rank="0",pp_rank="0",tp_rank="0"} 0.0` (the fixture's own line, indented) - engine_metrics resolves requests_running, guard says not sourced. INPUT, tab separator on the unlabelled branch: `sglang:num_running_reqs\t0.0` - parse_metrics -> [('sglang:num_running_reqs', {}, 0.0)], guard -> False. INPUT, leading tab and leading narrow no-break space: same divergence. Measured also and handled CORRECTLY: empty label set (`sglang:num_running_reqs{} 0.0`, both True), timestamp column, trailing comment, carriage return ending.

CHECKLIST 3 - expectations derived from the thing they check. Two remain. test_both_families_report_every_quantity_2y_publish lines 373 and 389 compare against _published() (line 219) and expected_vllm (lines 378-381), both built from engine_metrics.GAUGE_SERIES/COUNTER_SERIES. Demonstrated by doing it: popping 'requests_running' from GAUGE_SERIES leaves that test GREEN while the literal-expectation test reddens on the same removal.

CHECKLIST 4 - the stored scrape is still the authority. Confirmed by doing it: a canonical field dropped from a copy of the fixture reddens the field-set test, naming the field in both the unresolved and the unsourced list.

CHECKLIST 5 - naming. All four sweeps over tests/test_engine_metrics.py return nothing: plan/stage/sprint labels, ticket and issue references, changelog prose, author attribution. The retired plan-named selector appears nowhere in the tree (grep over tests/ and docs/ returns nothing) and no comment or caption cites the plan document.

SCORE goal_fidelity: 17
JUSTIFICATION goal_fidelity: both round-four findings are closed for their principal shapes and both close under my own hand rather than on the worker's account - the unlabelled branch reddens exactly one test under its recorded mutation and is green unmutated, and the declared control's receipt now names the revision under test and the selector as it runs today, so the selection error that made its predecessor vacuous is gone. The canonical field set is written out literally (lines 55-97) and re-asserts the served set offline. Docked three because the guard is not equivalent to the reader it guards (four accepted shapes refused, so its 'unsourced' verdict is not the reader's verdict) and because one expectation pair remains derived from the module tables.

SCORE evidence: 15
JUSTIFICATION evidence: the declared control reproduces and its assertion is specific rather than incidental, the two load-bearing receipts replay to their recorded counts verbatim, the fixture is byte-identical and unmutated, and the worktree is clean. Docked five because the receipt the manifest cites as the evidence for the unlabelled-branch restore reads NO for a restore that succeeded - its check runs before the restore - and the pre-fix receipt carries no restoration line at all while the manifest claims sha256 verification for it, so two of the run's three in-place mutations are evidenced by the final state and not by the receipt that is quoted for them. A reader of the log alone is told the opposite of the truth.

SCORE scope_discipline: 19
JUSTIFICATION scope_discipline: ca25efb8 touches only tests/test_engine_metrics.py and 7adfc3a3 only the two docs, both inside the node's declared write paths; the fixture blob is untouched; the commits carry conventional subjects with bodies; the worktree is clean and nothing was pushed. Docked one for the inherited, unchanged pin of the fixture's quiet zero (tests/test_engine_metrics.py:422), a value the node's own fixture-refresh follow-on must rewrite.

SCORE durability: 17
JUSTIFICATION durability: the pin is real and measured by me - neutralising line 130 turns exactly one test red at the recorded count, the file is 16 passed unmutated, and both spellings are now asserted independently, so a removal of the unlabelled branch cannot return unnoticed. Docked three because the guard's divergence means the file's own guarantee is conditional on the fixture being spelled the way the guard expects: an indented or tab-separated scrape reddens the test for a defect it does not have.

SCORE fit: 19
JUSTIFICATION fit: the naming sweeps over the file return nothing - no plan labels, deliverable IDs, ticket references, changelog prose, version suffixes or author attribution - the new test is named for the behaviour it holds, its docstring states the mechanism rather than a plan, and no comment or caption anywhere in the tree still cites the retired plan-named selector. Docked one because the docstring at lines 280-291 now claims 'Both spellings of a sample are covered' - I verified the two spellings tested ARE covered - but it states the value-token rule generally while the guard reads lines the reader accepts as no sample at all.

FINDING tests/test_engine_metrics.py:121 the guard refuses shapes the reader accepts: input ` sglang:num_running_reqs{...} 0.0` (leading space) and `sglang:num_running_reqs\t0.0` (bare tab, adopted by the it bare-leader application) both resolve through engine_metrics and both return False from _has_sample_line, so the test's unsourced verdict is not the reader's verdict.
FINDING neg-control-unlabelled-branch.log:71 the restoration line is a constant: it is emitted before the restore command runs, so it prints NO whatever the file holds, and the manifest's sha256 claim for that restore has no receipt behind it even though the restore did succeed.
